$comment: The indexes web_search may ask. Every key is documented in docs/pi-multi-search.md.
role          web | reference | papers | discussion | code — routing reads this, and the roles
a question earns are asked. `web` is always one of them.
priority      lower wins, and one index per role is asked by default, so a keyed index takes
over from the keyless one and falls back to it when its key is missing.
weight        0..1: how much the index's own ranking is trusted in the merge. Ranking quality,
not who paid. Measured: a 1.0 index beats a 0.8 index's rank 1 for its first 16
results, so only lower a weight for an index that deserves to lose every tie.
limit         results to ask this index for (default: defaults.limit).
shorten/retry `retryOnEmpty: true` retries once with the topic's core words when the index
came back empty (both Algolia and Stack Exchange match terms conjunctively).
shape         "none" opts a source out of query shaping.
**ONE SOURCE IS ENABLED IN THIS FILE: `duckduckgo`, because it is free and needs no key.** A
fresh install therefore answers, costs nothing and asks for no account — which is the only
honest default for a package someone just installed. Every other entry is here, defined and
tested, switched off. To turn one on: set `"enabled": true` at the top of its block, and for a
keyed one put the key in `~/.pi/agent/web-search.env` or your project's `.env` (a key whose
source is still disabled is reported in the footer rather than silently ignored).
kind absent   a built-in, by id: duckduckgo | wikipedia | hackernews | stackexchange.
kind json     a URL template ({query}, {limit}; http(s) only) plus `items`, `title`, `link`,
`snippet`, `date` — dot paths, where `a|b` means 'this, else that'. `date` takes
the first value that looks like an ISO date; prose ages are ignored.
kind rss|atom a feed: `<item>` or `<entry>`, title, link, and a body under one of four names.
method POST   sends a JSON `body` whose values are templated the same way, and `"{limit}"`
becomes a number. A POST source may keep {query} in the body instead of the URL.
key           the NAME of an environment variable (never a literal); `keyHeader` says where it
goes (default `Authorization: Bearer`). The variable is read from the process
environment, `envFile` if the profile names one, then ./.env, then
~/.pi/agent/web-search.env. A keyed source with no key is skipped, and the footer
names the missing variable.
A bad entry refuses to load, by name, rather than returning nothing forever.

wikipedia.$why: Free and keyless. Off by default so a fresh install asks one index; turn it on for a `reference` opinion on definition questions.

hackernews.$why: Free and keyless. Off by default; turn it on for `discussion` on comparisons and release news.

stackexchange.$why: Free and keyless. Off by default; this is the one worth turning on first if you ask a lot of code questions — it is the specialist the `code` role routes to.

arxiv.$why: Free and keyless. Off by default; turn it on for `papers` if you ask about research.

marginalia.$why: A keyless HTML endpoint whose shape is not stable; enable only with a parser, not a template.
marginalia.title: title

brave.$why: Keyed, and worth it: 2 000 searches/month free. Put BRAVE_API_KEY in ~/.pi/agent/web-search.env or ./.env, then set "enabled": true here.
brave.title: title

tavily.$why: Keyed. Put TAVILY_API_KEY in ~/.pi/agent/web-search.env or ./.env, then set "enabled": true here. `search_depth: advanced` costs 2 credits instead of 1.
tavily.title: title
